pr_body:
1, set_inertia shouldn't check for >0, since a value <=0 means erasing custom inertia
2, Add a variable to save custom inertia
3, only update inertia when it's needed when change mode
4, reset angular velocity to 0 when switching to character mode
closes #30838

issue_context.title: set_inertia on RigidBody2D to greater than zero prevents set_mode from working correctly
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.1.1 stable official


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 Home


**Issue description:**
When using set_inertia on a RigidBody2D setting anything greater than zero prevents set_mode from working correctly.
Specifically: if in MODE_CHARACTER and set_mode(RigidBody2D.MODE_RIGID) is used the MODE flag changes to MODE_RIGID but the body continues to act as MODE_CHARACTER.
Note that by removing the first set_inertia instruction from the script (the one that sets inertia to a very small value >0) all then works fine.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Run the NODE2D scene in the attached project, press "down arrow" which should switch the RigidBody2D from Character to Rigid. The mode flag changes but the body`s behaviour does not. The body should start to rotate as torque is being applied.
You can check the current mode and inertia by pressing "Enter". Press 'Up Arrow" to switch back to rigid mode.


**Minimal reproduction project:**
[rigidbodybug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3435819/rigidbodybug.zip)
comments: Changing mode to MODE_RIGID_CHARACTER, MODE_STATIC and MODE_KINEMATIC will clear custom inertia value, so resetting inertia after you switch to MODE_RIGID is a temporarily solution, I'm solving this.

Thanks  Raphael, sadly the work around does not seem to work for me. 
Possibly I am doing something wrong, do you have a working example by any chance?

Incidentally is there a reason why get_inertia can return zero but set_inertia(0) returns an error? IE:
(E 0:00:06:0689   Condition ' p_inertia <= 0 ' is true.
  <C Source>     scene/2d/physics_body_2d.cpp:607 @ set_inertia()
  <Stack Trace>  RigidBody2D.gd:11 @ _integrate_forces()

Write it like that :
`set_mode(Rigidbody2D.MODE_RIGID)
set_inertia(1)`
Seems the code forget that inertia can be a value <= 0, so `set_inertia(0)` cause errors,  I'll delete the checking.

Sorry Raphael but it still seems to do the same, the code in my example now looks like this:
```extends RigidBody2D

func _ready():
	set_inertia(1)

func _process(delta):
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up") and get_mode() != RigidBody2D.MODE_CHARACTER: 
		print("MODE BEFORE: ", get_mode())
		set_mode(RigidBody2D.MODE_CHARACTER)
		set_inertia(1)
		set_angular_velocity(0)
		set_rotation(0)
		print("MODE AFTER: ", get_mode())
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down") and get_mode() != RigidBody2D.MODE_RIGID: 
		print("MODE BEFORE: ", get_mode())
		set_mode(RigidBody2D.MODE_RIGID)
		set_inertia(1)
		set_angular_velocity(0)
		set_rotation(0)
		print("MODE AFTER: ", get_mode())
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_accept"):
		print("MODE NOW: " , get_mode(), " Inertia: ", inertia, " angular_velocity: ", angular_velocity, " rotation: ", rotation) 

func _integrate_forces(state):
	set_applied_torque(10)
```

Still seems to go into RIGID and never go back to CHARACTER.
Perhaps I can work around by manually simulating character mode, any tips on what settings I would have to manually fix? (very high inertia perhaps, zero rotational velocity?)

Thanks for the help, 
Giles

Write it like this :
```extends RigidBody2D

	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up") and get_mode() != RigidBody2D.MODE_CHARACTER: 
		print("MODE BEFORE: ", get_mode())

		print(get_inertia())

	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down") and get_mode() != RigidBody2D.MODE_RIGID: 
		print("MODE BEFORE: ", get_mode())
		set_mode(RigidBody2D.MODE_RIGID)
		set_applied_torque(1000)
		set_inertia(10)
		print("MODE AFTER: ", get_mode())
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_accept"):
		print("MODE NOW: " , get_mode(), " Inertia: ", get_inertia())```

That will only work until it interacts with some other physics object, the actual character mode does not allow any rotation even if you apply torque manually.
Don`t worry, I`ll try to figure out how to simulate character mode by experimentation.

review_comments: Does it make sense to set a negative inertia?

According to this https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.1/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html#class-rigidbody2d-property-inertia , a negative inertia means erasing user custom inertia and recalculate it.
Maybe we should use another param like `custom_inertia` to control it? If so, we can keep in same with setting custom gravity center in the future, since you can't set a "negative gravity center".
I think the "(or negative)" part of the documentation should simply be removed, setting it to 0 is sufficient for a way to erase the custom inertia.

So how about adding a bool param `use_custom_inertia` to control it ?
If we add it, this will be same mechanism with `custom_gravity_center`(future feature) , 
you can't use a zero value meaning erase custom gravity center(zero means a custom gravity center at origin position).

Well I prefer not future proofing the API, we can do these changes if we do add a way to override the gravity center. Until this, it's better to keep the API unchanged in this PR and just fix the issue.
